releases.summary: Careers application functions: tested, and two weaknesses fixed before they go live
changes: Both Edge Functions (careers-apply, careers-confirm) were run for the first time, offline, against stand-ins for Supabase, Resend and Cloudflare: 38 checks pass (validation, bot check, closed/draft/expired jobs, the 3-per-hour limit, the full success path, failure clean-up, confirm, already-confirmed). The tests are saved at supabase/functions/_tests/careers-harness.ts. Both also pass Deno's type-check

careers-apply: if the confirmation email cannot be sent (Resend refuses it, is unreachable, or the Resend secrets are missing) the application is no longer saved as a dead end that says "check your email". The half-finished application and its resume are removed and the applicant sees a clear message to check the address and try again. Missing email settings now refuse up front (503) instead of saving silently

careers-confirm: opening the link in the email now only shows a "Confirm my email" button, and pressing it (a POST) does the confirming. Before, any program that merely opened the link, such as a mail scanner, would have marked the address confirmed
Nothing is deployed yet and the application form still reads "Applications open soon"; the functions are not live

releases.summary: Careers: the Cloudflare Turnstile bot-check site key is now in the site config
changes: js/careers-config.js: turnstileSiteKey is set (a public value). The widget is registered in Cloudflare for www.takgio.com and takgio.com in Managed mode. The key was checked with Cloudflare's own widget: a correct key on an unregistered address returns 110200 (domain not authorized), a mistyped key returns 400020 (invalid sitekey)
No visible change yet: applyUrl is still empty, so the application form keeps showing "Applications open soon" until the careers-apply function is deployed and its secrets are set

releases.summary: Careers admin: the "no access" screen now says which account you are signed in as, and a failed access check shows its error
changes: When a signed-in account has no row in careers_editors, the screen now reads "You're signed in as <email>, but that account hasn't been given access" and suggests trying another account. Before, it only said "this account", which hid that a person had signed in with a different login than the one granted
If the access lookup itself fails (permissions, network), the page now shows "Couldn't check your access" with the error text, instead of treating the failure as "no access"
Checked against the stand-in sign-in: no access, a failed lookup, and the normal admin path

releases.summary: Fix: the Careers admin showed a blank page in browsers with an ad or content blocker
changes: careers-admin.html, js/careers-admin.js and css/careers-admin.css named every class and the page root with an "ad-" prefix (ad-body, ad-root, ad-login and so on, short for "admin"). Content blockers treat "ad-" names as advertising and hide them: in Ted's Chrome and Brave the whole page was clipped to nothing (clip-path: inset(100%) on the body) while the sign-in and authenticator screens were actually there, invisible. Renaming <body class="ad-body"> alone removed the clip in a live test
Every "ad-" class and id in those three files is now "cra-" (cra-body, cra-root, cra-login and so on): 225 occurrences, no other file used them. No behaviour change

Checked in Ted's own Chrome from the local server (page visible, clip-path none) and against the stand-in sign-in for the code screen, first-time authenticator enrolment, no-access, and the Jobs, Applications, Team and Post-a-job screens

releases.summary: Fix: a password-reset link now opens the Reset Password form instead of jumping to the dashboard
changes: login.html: a reset (recovery) link from email signs the person in, and the page's "already signed in, go to the dashboard" redirect then won the race, so the Reset Password form flashed and vanished and no password could be set. The page now notices it was opened from a recovery link (type=recovery in the URL) and skips that redirect while the reset form is showing (js/auth.js)
New: login.html?reset=1 shows the same Reset Password form to someone who is already signed in, so a password can be set or changed without waiting for another email
A plain visit to login.html while signed in still goes to the dashboard, and a visitor with no session still sees the normal sign-in form (both checked)
